job.title: Clinical Project Manager Oncology OR General Medicine - Based North Carolina
job.description:
Are you an experienced Clinical Project Manager with Oncology and/or General Medicine experience looking for a role where you can take genuine ownership of international clinical studies while remaining closely involved in the operational delivery of clinical trials?

We are partnering with a leading global Contract Research Organisation (CRO) to appoint an experienced Clinical Project Manager to oversee the successful delivery of international clinical trials from study startup through to closeout.

Working as the primary point of contact for sponsors, you will lead project planning, execution, financial oversight, and cross functional collaboration to ensure studies are delivered on time, within budget and in compliance with ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, and internal quality standards.

This opportunity is suited to a proactive project leader with excellent stakeholder management skills, commercial awareness, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while driving operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

Project Leadership

  • Lead end to end delivery of global clinical studies, from feasibility and site selection through to database lock and study close out.
  • Develop and maintain project plans, timelines, risk registers and study tracking tools.
  • Coordinate cross functional teams across Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Biometrics, Medical, Pharmacovigillance, and Vendor Management.
  • Proactively identify project risks and implement mitigation strategies to support successful study delivery.
  • Ensure projects are conducted in accordance with study protocols, ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, and company SOPs.

Client & Stakeholder Management
 
  • Act as the primary point of contact for sponsors throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Build strong client relationships through regular communication, project updates and proactive issue resolution.
  • Lead project meetings, governance calls, and support business development activities, including bid defence meetings where required.
  • Partner with commercial teams during feasibility assessments and change order discussions.
Financial & Operational Management
 
  • Manage project budgets, revenue forecasts, profitability, and overall financial performance.
  • Monitor project scope and coordinate change orders where appropriate.
  • Ensure effective project resourcing and workload planning.
  • Oversee external vendors and service providers to ensure high-quality delivery.
Site & Study Management
  • Oversee site selection, activation, patient recruitment, monitoring, and study close-out activities.
  • Support ethics and regulatory submissions in collaboration with Clinical Operations and Regulatory teams.
  • Monitor recruitment performance and implement strategies to optimise enrolment and site productivity.
  • Maintain inspection and audit readiness throughout the study lifecycle.
Leadership & Continuous Improvement
 
  • Provide leadership, mentoring, and support to cross-functional project teams, including Associate Project Managers where applicable.
  • Foster a collaborative, accountable, and high performing project environment.
  • Contribute to process improvements, SOP development, and operational excellence initiatives.
  • Represent the organisation professionally with sponsors, investigators, and external stakeholders.

About You
  • You are an experienced clinical project leader with excellent organisational, leadership and communications skills. You enjoy working in a collaborative, fast paced environment and are passionate about delivering high quality clinical research while building trusted relationships with sponsors and study teams.

Qualifications & Experience
 
  • Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, or a related discipline.
  • Significant clinical project management experience ideally within Oncology or General Medicine and within a CRO Pharmaceutical, or biotechnology environment.
  • Strong understanding of the end to end clinical trial lifecycle, including study start up, site management, patient recruitment, data management and study close out.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of ICH-GCP, global clinical trial regulations, and sponsor requirements
  • Proven experience managing global, cross-functional project teams, budgets, timelines, and project risks.
  • Demonstrated client-facing experience with the ability to develop long-term sponsor relationships.
  • Experience using CTMS, eTMF, Microsoft Office, and other clinical trial management systems.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

job.title: Senior Legal Counsel based North Carolina
job.description:
Quiddity Talent Solutions is partnering with a leading global Clinical Research Organisation (CRO) to appoint an experienced Senior Legal Counsel to join its growing US legal team in North Carolina.

This is a senior in-house legal opportunity supporting a growing US business within a global life sciences organisation. Working across a broad range of legal matters—including commercial contracts, corporate governance, employment, compliance, privacy and strategic projects—you'll provide practical legal guidance that helps the business operate confidently and compliantly.

You'll be a key legal partner to senior leaders across the organisation, offering commercially focused advice on complex legal and contractual issues. The role is suited to someone who enjoys balancing legal risk with business priorities and influencing decision-making within a collaborative, international environment.

Key Responsibilities Include:

•    Manage the full lifecycle of commercial contracts, from drafting and negotiation through to execution, across a variety of customer, supplier, consultancy, confidentiality and collaboration agreements.
•    Provide practical, commercially focused legal guidance to the business on a wide range of matters, including commercial contracts, corporate governance, employment, compliance, privacy and day-to-day operational issues.
•    Work closely with commercial, clinical and corporate functions to identify legal and contractual risks and develop appropriate solutions that support business objectives.
•    Support the resolution of disputes, regulatory enquiries, employment matters and internal investigations, engaging external legal advisers where appropriate.
•    Advise on mergers, acquisitions and other strategic corporate transactions, providing legal support through due diligence, transaction execution and post-acquisition integration activities.
•    Help shape and enhance internal legal policies, compliance processes and enterprise risk management practices.
•    Provide advice on data privacy and information governance requirements across international markets.
•    Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, acting as a strategic legal partner to the wider business.
•    Collaborate with an international legal team to deliver consistent, high-quality legal support across multiple regions and business functions.


About you 

We're interested in speaking with qualified lawyers who bring:

•    Approximately 10 + years post qualification experience gained in private practice, in-house, or a combination of both.
•    Strong experience negotiating and drafting complex commercial agreements.
•    Experience providing legal support within global organisations operating across multiple international markets.
•    A background within life sciences, clinical research, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or healthcare.
•    Excellent stakeholder management, communication and negotiation skills.
•    A commercially minded approach to providing practical legal advice while effectively managing business risk.

What's on Offer

•    Hybrid working based in North Carolina.
•    Opportunity to join a collaborative global legal team within a growing international life sciences organisation.
•    Broad exposure to commercial, operational and strategic legal work across the US business.
•    Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.

job.title: Sourcing Lead - Talent Acquisition Partner Based Madrid
job.description:
We have been engaged by a leading global Clinical Research Organisation to appoint an experienced Sourcing Lead / Specialist  Resourcer to support its Talent Acquisition team in Madrid.

This is a dedicated sourcing role supporting recruitment across a broad FSP portfolio, identifying and engaging high-quality talent across a range of clinical research and life sciences positions.

Working closely with the wider Talent Acquisition team, you will take ownership of candidate sourcing and pipeline development, helping ensure recruiters and hiring teams have access to strong, relevant talent across multiple searches.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Proactively source and engage candidates across a range of FSP and clinical research positions.
  • Build targeted talent pipelines for both current and anticipated hiring requirements.
  • Use LinkedIn, databases, professional networks and other sourcing channels to identify relevant talent.
  • Conduct initial candidate outreach and qualification conversations.
  • Maintain accurate candidate and recruitment information within Workday.
  • Work closely with Talent Acquisition colleagues to understand role priorities and candidate profiles.
  • Provide market insight around candidate availability, competitor activity and talent pools.
  • Deliver a professional and engaging candidate experience throughout the sourcing process.
  • Support multiple searches simultaneously within a fast-moving international recruitment environment.

What We’re Looking For

We are particularly interested in speaking with experienced Resourcers, Talent Sourcers or Recruitment Consultants who enjoy the candidate identification and engagement side of recruitment.

Ideally, you will bring:

  • Previous sourcing or recruitment experience within life sciences, clinical research, pharmaceutical, biotech, healthcare or a related sector.
  • Strong experience using LinkedIn and other direct sourcing methods.
  • Confidence approaching and engaging passive candidates.
  • Experience working with an ATS; Workday experience would be particularly useful.
  • The ability to manage multiple sourcing projects and priorities.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively as part of an international Talent Acquisition team.
  • Professional fluency in English.

Spanish does not need to be your first language, although you will need to be comfortable working from the Madrid office 2–3 days per week.

This would suit someone who enjoys the research and sourcing element of recruitment and wants to work within a highly established global clinical research organisation, supporting a varied and evolving portfolio of hiring activity.

job.title: Portfolio Director Immunology and Infectious Disease Based US
job.description:
Portfolio Director – Immunology & Infectious Disease | United States

We are supporting a global CRO with the appointment of an experienced Portfolio Director to lead a portfolio of clinical development programmes across Immunology & Infectious Disease in the US.

This is a senior leadership role combining clinical operations, portfolio strategy, client leadership and business growth. You will oversee a team of Project Directors and Project Managers while taking ownership of the performance, development and continued growth of the portfolio.

The opportunity

You will work closely with Therapeutic Area leadership, Medical & Scientific Strategy and Business Development teams to shape operational strategy, strengthen existing client relationships and support the award of new and repeat business.

Key responsibilities will include:

• Leading the delivery and performance of multiple complex clinical development programmes
• Growing the Immunology & Infectious Disease portfolio through proposals, bid defences and strategic client engagement
• Acting as a senior relationship lead for key clients and proactively identifying opportunities to strengthen partnerships
• Coaching and developing Project Directors and Project Managers
• Overseeing portfolio KPIs including timelines, quality, financial performance and client satisfaction
• Managing portfolio-level risk and ensuring appropriate mitigation strategies are implemented
• Working cross-functionally with Clinical Operations, Medical & Scientific Strategy, Business Development and Finance
• Supporting the longer-term strategy and development of the Immunology & Infectious Disease Therapeutic Area
• Ensuring projects are delivered in accordance with ICH-GCP and relevant regulatory requirements

What we are looking for

We are interested in speaking with senior clinical development leaders who combine strong operational delivery experience with genuine commercial and client-facing capability.

You will ideally bring:

• Significant clinical research and clinical project/portfolio leadership experience within a CRO, biotech or pharmaceutical environment
• Strong experience leading complex global clinical programmes
• Demonstrable expertise within Immunology and/or Infectious Disease
• Experience managing and developing senior Project Management teams
• A strong understanding of clinical development, ICH-GCP and regulatory requirements
• Proven client relationship management and stakeholder leadership skills
• Experience contributing to proposals, bid defences and new business growth
• Strong financial and commercial acumen, including portfolio budgeting and forecasting
• The ability to operate strategically while remaining close enough to delivery to identify and resolve issues early

This position would particularly suit someone who has moved beyond managing individual studies and is now looking to take broader ownership of a therapeutic portfolio, senior client relationships and business growth.

 

If you would like to discuss the opportunity confidentially, please contact the Quiddity Talent Solutions team or apply directly.

job.title: Head of Project Management CNS/Neuroscience Based US
job.description:
CNS drug development demands a different kind of leadership. The science is complex, the patient populations are underserved, and the operational stakes are high. This organisation is looking for a Head of Project Management to take executive ownership of its CNS & Neuroscience Therapeutic Area  driving both the strategic growth of the practice and the delivery of complex, multi-jurisdictional clinical programmes.

This is a portfolio-level leadership role with accountability for client relationships at accounts exceeding $75 million in backlog, a direct team of Portfolio Directors, Project Oversight Directors, and Project Managers, and a mandate to grow the book of business alongside operational excellence.

The Role

Therapeutic Area Growth

  • Lead proposal strategy and bid defence for new CNS/Neuroscience business, working closely with Business Development and Medical & Scientific Strategists to develop compelling operational plans.
  • Oversee the development and maintenance of therapeutic playbooks, white papers, scientific advisory panels, and service offerings  ensuring the practice remains at the leading edge of the field.
  • Forecast resources and lead targeted hiring for specialists with relevant trial methodology and investigational product expertise.
  • Nominate and align Portfolio Directors, Project Oversight Directors, and Global Project Managers for incoming accounts in collaboration with workforce planning.

Executive Oversight & Delivery

  • Provide executive oversight across multiple clinical development portfolios within the Therapeutic Area, ensuring alignment with client strategic goals and ICH-GCP requirements.
  • Act as Executive Sponsor for nominated accounts; lead client governance meetings and provide senior-level updates on performance, risks, and mitigation.
  • Monitor KPIs across delivery timelines, financial health, and client satisfaction — and drive corrective action where needed.
  • Identify, assess, and mitigate risks at Therapeutic Area level, implementing preventive and corrective actions in line with internal and external policy.

Leadership & People

  • Manage and develop a team of Portfolio Directors, Project Oversight Directors, and Project Delivery Directors — providing guidance, coaching, and genuine career development.
  • Foster a high-performing culture built on collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure optimal resource allocation and utilisation across the Therapeutic Area in alignment with business needs.

Strategy & Financial Oversight

  • Collaborate with the SVP, Global Project Management to contribute to the strategic direction of the function and the Therapeutic Area's long-term plan.
  • Oversee the financial performance of the Therapeutic Area — budgeting, forecasting, and profitability — working with Finance and senior leadership on accurate reporting.
  • Drive initiatives to optimise processes, improve efficiency, and meet (or exceed) growth targets.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's or advanced degree in Life Sciences, Clinical Research, or a related field.
  • 15+ years in clinical research, with at least 10 years in project or portfolio management roles in a global environment.
  • A background that spans biotech, pharma, and CRO environments — ideally with deep CNS/Neuroscience expertise across multiple programme types.
  • Strong command of ICH-GCP and applicable regulatory requirements across major markets.
  • A proven track record leading large, complex cross-functional programmes and managing senior client relationships at scale.
  • Commercially minded — with demonstrable experience in business development activities including bid defence and proposal strategy.
  • Financial acumen: experience managing budgets and financial performance at a portfolio or practice level.
  • Exceptional communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

job.title: Therapeutic Strategy Lead CNS Based US
job.description:
Therapeutic Strategy Lead – CNS

Location: United States
Therapeutic Area: CNS
Function: Therapeutic Strategy / Clinical Development / Medical Strategy
Employment Type: Full-time

About the Role

We are supporting the appointment of a Therapeutic Strategy Lead – CNS for a senior US-based opportunity within a global clinical research environment.

This is a strategic, client-facing role for an experienced CNS clinical development professional who can provide deep therapeutic and scientific expertise across clinical programme design, study feasibility, site and KOL engagement, and proposal development.

The Therapeutic Strategy Lead will act as a senior subject-matter expert within CNS, partnering closely with business development, clinical operations, medical, regulatory and strategy teams to design scientifically robust, operationally feasible and commercially aligned clinical programmes.

This role would suit someone who combines strong scientific credibility with practical clinical trial delivery understanding and the ability to translate complex therapeutic insight into clear, actionable development strategy.

Key Responsibilities

The Therapeutic Strategy Lead will provide senior scientific and therapeutic leadership across CNS clinical development activities.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Providing CNS therapeutic and scientific input into protocol design, study feasibility, clinical development planning and scientific advisory discussions.
  • Supporting client-facing proposals, RFP responses, bid defences and early study concept development.
  • Translating CNS therapeutic insight into clear study rationale, risk assessment, mitigation planning and competitive landscape analysis.
  • Building and maintaining strong relationships with academic KOLs, principal investigators and high-performing clinical sites.
  • Supporting investigator identification and site selection strategies to improve enrolment, delivery quality and data integrity.
  • Advising cross-functional teams on endpoint selection, regulatory considerations, comparator standards, safety monitoring and operational feasibility.
  • Working closely with business development, medical, clinical operations, regulatory, safety and clinical teams to ensure programmes are strategically sound and executable.
  • Contributing to budget, timeline, monitoring and vendor considerations from a therapeutic and operational perspective.
  • Mentoring and upskilling internal colleagues on CNS clinical development, therapeutic area trends and best practice.
  • Supporting thought leadership and capability building across the organisation.

CNS Expertise

The successful candidate will bring strong expertise across CNS clinical development. Relevant experience may include areas such as neurology, psychiatry, neurodegenerative disorders, movement disorders, rare neurological disease, pain, sleep disorders or other CNS-related indications.

They will understand the scientific, regulatory and operational complexity often associated with CNS studies, including patient identification, endpoint selection, study design, site engagement, enrolment challenges and the importance of robust clinical assessment strategies.

Candidate Profile

We are seeking a credible and commercially aware CNS therapeutic expert with strong clinical development experience and the ability to influence both internal and external stakeholders.

The ideal candidate will bring:

  • An advanced clinical or scientific degree, such as MD, PhD, PharmD or equivalent.
  • Significant industry experience in clinical development, ideally including late-stage programme leadership or therapeutic strategy roles.
  • Strong CNS therapeutic area expertise and scientific credibility with clinical, academic and investigator communities.
  • Experience contributing to study design, feasibility, proposal development, bid defence or client-facing scientific strategy.
  • The ability to balance scientific rigour with operational feasibility, commercial priorities and sponsor expectations.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex science into clear development strategy.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with clinical operations, business development, regulatory, medical, safety and commercial teams.
  • Strong understanding of global clinical trial delivery, regulatory expectations and current standards of care.
  • A collaborative, influential and externally credible style.

Key Attributes

This role will suit someone who is:

  • Strategic and scientifically curious.
  • Confident in front of clients, investigators and internal senior stakeholders.
  • Able to combine therapeutic expertise with practical delivery insight.
  • Commercially aware and comfortable supporting business growth.
  • Skilled at building trusted relationships with KOLs, sites and cross-functional teams.
  • Comfortable working in a global, matrixed clinical research environment.
  • Passionate about improving clinical development strategy within CNS.

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity for a senior CNS clinical development professional to take on a highly visible therapeutic strategy role with broad influence across clinical programme design, client engagement and operational delivery.

The role offers the opportunity to shape CNS development strategy, strengthen external KOL and site relationships, support high-quality clinical trial design and contribute directly to business growth within a global clinical research setting.

job.title: Associate Manager Regulatory Affairs Based North Carolina
job.description:
Associate Manager – Regulatory Affairs / Regulatory Operations North Carolina

Location: North Carolina, USA
Sector: CRO / Clinical Research
Salary: $110,000 – $145,000 depending on experience

About the Opportunity

Quiddity Talent Solutions is supporting a global clinical research organisation with the appointment of an Associate Manager within Regulatory Affairs / Regulatory Operations in North Carolina.

This is an opportunity for an experienced regulatory professional to combine operational regulatory expertise with team leadership, supporting the successful start-up and delivery of clinical trials.

You will provide oversight and guidance to Regulatory Start-Up colleagues, helping ensure regulatory authority and ethics committee submissions, approvals and site identification activities are delivered efficiently and in accordance with ICH-GCP, local regulatory requirements and company procedures.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide day-to-day leadership, mentoring and support to Regulatory Start-Up team members.

  • Oversee the preparation, review and submission of Regulatory Authority and Ethics Committee applications.

  • Support timely clinical trial approvals and study start-up activities.

  • Review essential study documentation including participant information and informed consent materials.

  • Provide regulatory input into study start-up timelines and project plans.

  • Act as a local regulatory subject matter expert, advising project teams on regulatory and ethics requirements.

  • Maintain oversight of regulatory activities, timelines and functional performance metrics.

  • Build effective relationships with internal project teams, clients and relevant third-party vendors.

  • Support continuous improvement across regulatory start-up processes and ways of working.

  • Contribute regulatory expertise to proposals, bid discussions and wider business development activities where required.

About You

We are looking for someone with a strong background in clinical regulatory affairs, regulatory operations or clinical study start-up within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology or CRO environment.

You will ideally bring:

  • A degree in clinical sciences, pharmacy, life sciences or a related discipline.

  • Strong knowledge of clinical regulatory and study start-up processes.

  • Experience supporting or managing Regulatory Authority and Ethics Committee submissions.

  • Previous mentoring, supervision or line-management experience.

  • Strong project management and organisational skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder-management capability.

  • A collaborative approach with the confidence to provide regulatory guidance to cross-functional teams.

This is a strong opportunity for someone looking to combine hands-on regulatory expertise with increased leadership responsibility within an international clinical research environment.

job.title: Medical Team Lead Based Perth, Australia
job.description:
Medical Team Lead – Early Phase Clinical Trials 

Location: Perth, Western Australia

Salary: AUD $200,000–$250,000 + Super + Salary Packaging

Work Pattern: Primarily Monday–Friday, 7:30am–3:30pm, with minimal on-call requirements and occasional weekend cover

 

We are recruiting for a leading Australian clinical research organisation for a newly created Medical Team Lead position within its growing Early Phase Unit (EPU).

This is a hands-on operational medical leadership role, reporting to the Medical Director and acting as the second-in-command (2IC) for the medical team. You will provide day-to-day clinical leadership, people management and operational oversight, while serving as the primary escalation point for medical matters within the Early Phase Unit.

The organisation partners with global pharmaceutical, biotechnology and academic sponsors to deliver high-quality clinical trials. The Early Phase Unit is a therapeutic-agnostic Phase I/II facility with a strong track record in delivering internationally funded clinical research.

This is an exiiting opportunity to work at the forefront of early-phase clinical science while enjoying a structured working environment and a sustainable alternative to the intensity of traditional hospital medicine.
 

Why Consider This Role?

  • Work at the cutting edge of early-phase clinical research, across a broad range of therapeutic areas
  • Join an internationally focused organisation working with pharmaceutical, biotech and academic sponsors
  • Enjoy a structured Monday–Friday working pattern, with minimal on-call and no ED-style emergency work
  • Lead a collaborative, non-hierarchical and highly experienced medical team
  • Take on a genuine leadership role within a growing Early Phase Unit
  • Be part of an organisation experiencing significant growth and expansion
  • Benefit from salary packaging available through the not-for-profit structure
  • Relocation support is available for the right candidate
 

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Leadership

  • Act as the first escalation point for operational medical matters within the Early Phase Unit
  • Oversee day-to-day medical services, roster coverage and team performance
  • Provide medical supervision and support to Research Physicians and medical students

Principal Investigator Responsibilities

  • Serve as Principal Investigator on clinical trials as required, with responsibility for overall trial conduct
  • Conduct and oversee participant consent, screening, dosing and follow-up procedures
  • Review and authorise clinical assessments, adverse events and study reports
  • Ensure clinical activities are delivered in accordance with ICH-GCP and applicable regulatory requirements

People Leadership

  • Lead, coach and develop Senior Research Physicians and Research Physicians
  • Drive performance, accountability and professional development across the medical team
  • Foster a collaborative, transparent and high-performing team culture

Operational & Project Management

  • Work closely with Recruitment and Screening teams to support enrolment targets
  • Contribute to protocol review, study start-up and continuous quality improvement
  • Support the efficient delivery of multiple concurrent early-phase clinical trials

 

About You

You are a qualified medical practitioner who brings clinical trial experience and a genuine interest in medical leadership and early-phase research.

You may be an experienced clinician looking to step away from the intensity of the traditional health system, or an established clinical research professional ready to take the next step into a broader leadership role.

What matters most is your clinical credibility, experience in clinical trials and ability to lead and develop people.

Essential Requirements

  • MBBS or equivalent medical qualification
  • Current AHPRA registration
  • Experience as a Principal Investigator and/or Sub-Investigator in clinical trials
  • Working knowledge of ICH-GCP and applicable clinical trial regulations
  • Demonstrated people leadership experience, including coaching, mentoring and performance management
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Ability to thrive in a collaborative, non-hierarchical environment
  • Eligible to work in Australia

Desirable Experience

  • Background in pharmacology, pharmaceutical medicine or early-phase research
  • Experience working within a Phase I/II Early Phase Unit or CRO environment
  • Experience managing PI responsibilities across multiple concurrent clinical trials
  • Commercial or growth-stage clinical research experience
  • Based in Perth, WA, or genuinely open to relocation

What’s on Offer

  • AUD $200,000–$250,000 base salary
  • Superannuation on top of base salary
  • Salary packaging through a not-for-profit organisation
  • 5 weeks annual leave
  • Relocation support available
  • Professional development and CPD support
  • Primarily Monday–Friday working hours
